fields.description:
## Problem

An async `verify_completion` run that FAILs returns `findings: null` from
`gate_status(job_id)`. The caller learns only that the gate failed, never why.
A failed `review_plan` job instead returns a populated `findings` descriptor
pointing at its `REVIEW_RESULT` sidecar.

Observed this session on `cfe0-4b2b`, and again on `f3b2-6bb8`:

```
{"status": "failed", "gate_type": "verify_completion",
 "findings": null, "verdict": "FAIL"}
```

The `COMPLETION_VERDICT` sidecar carrying the real findings HAD been written and
was readable by hand from the tickets branch. The data was never discarded. It
was never surfaced.

Cost: reading a completion FAIL's reason requires hand-reading the tickets
branch, or a duplicate billable gate pass.

## Root cause

Three plan-review-only narrowings on one call-graph seam.

1. `src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:201-203` — `_review_result_status()` returns `None`
   unless `gate_type == _PLAN_REVIEW`. `gate_run_status()` at
   `src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:316-318` sets `out["findings"]` only when that
   helper returns non-None, so the key is absent for every completion run. This
   is the visible symptom.

2. Neither correlation field reaches a completion index record.
   `sidecar_emitted` is stamped by the CALLER on the plan-review path
   (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/__init__.py:578`,
   `verdict["sidecar_emitted"] = sidecar.emit(...)`). The completion caller
   `record_completion_verdict` does not do this: at
   `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:189` it binds
   `sidecar_written = completion_sidecar.emit(result, ...)` into a local and
   returns it inside a separate `_outcome` dict at
   `src/rebar/_commands/transition_close.py:198-199`, never writing
   `result["sidecar_emitted"]`. `sidecar_reviewed_at` has no completion writer at
   all: `completion_sidecar.emit()` returns a bare `bool` and discards the
   timestamp `append_event` returns.

3. No `COMPLETION_VERDICT` timestamp reader exists.
   `_latest_review_result_timestamp` (`src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:154-158`)
   delegates to `plan_review.sidecar.latest_review_timestamp`
   (`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/sidecar.py:263`). `completion_sidecar` exposes
   only `latest_fail_verdict`, `latest_pass_record` and `latest_screen_tally`,
   which return verdict dicts, not an `int` timestamp.

Correlation by timestamp is what makes the descriptor trustworthy. Reporting the
newest `COMPLETION_VERDICT` for the ticket without it would attribute a prior
run's findings to this job.

## Design

`completion_sidecar.py`. `_append_sidecar_retrying()` returns the timestamp
`append_event` returns. `emit()` stamps BOTH fields on the verdict dict it
already receives as its first parameter: `verdict["sidecar_emitted"]` on every
path, `verdict["sidecar_reviewed_at"]` only on a successful append. The stamping
goes inside `emit()` rather than in its caller — the plan-review placement —
because `transition_close.py:189` keeps the bool in a local that never returns to
the verdict. Mutation is visible to the daemon: `_record_verify_completion`
(`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:50-69`) passes that same dict to `record_completion_verdict`
then returns it, and `_spawn_gate_daemon` reads `result` at
`src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py:168`. `emit()` keeps its `bool` return, so no caller changes.

Add `latest_verdict_timestamp(ticket_id, *, repo_root)` to `completion_sidecar`,
mirroring `plan_review/sidecar.py:263`: it reads the ns prefix of
`<ts>-<uuid>-COMPLETION_VERDICT.json` filenames, needs no JSON parse, and returns
`None` on any error. This supplies the completion timestamp source.

`_mcp_llm.py`. Rename `_plan_review_sidecar_fields` to `_gate_sidecar_fields` and
widen its guard to admit `verify_completion` alongside `plan_review`. Its body
already reads exactly the two fields now stamped.

`gate_runs.py`. Add `_COMPLETION_VERDICT = "COMPLETION_VERDICT"`. Parameterise
`_latest_review_result_timestamp` by a latest-timestamp reader, and
`_has_review_result_timestamp` by sidecar kind plus accepted schema set.
`_review_result_status` resolves gate type through a module-level mapping —
`plan_review` to `REVIEW_RESULT` with `{plan_review_result_v1,
plan_review_result_v2}` and `latest_review_timestamp`; `verify_completion` to
`COMPLETION_VERDICT` with `{completion_verifier_pass_v1,
completion_verifier_fail_v1}` and `latest_verdict_timestamp` — returning `None`
for any other gate type, which preserves today's behaviour for `code_review`. Its
`sidecar_type` output field reports the resolved kind.

The mapping is a module-level table, not added branches, so each touched function
stays under its complexity ceiling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failed async `verify_completion` job returns a non-null `findings` object from `gate_status`.
- [ ] That `findings` object reports `sidecar_type` as `COMPLETION_VERDICT`.
- [ ] That `findings` object reports `readable` as `true` when a matching sidecar exists.
- [ ] A passed async `verify_completion` job returns a non-null `findings` object.
- [ ] `completion_sidecar.emit()` stamps `sidecar_reviewed_at` on the verdict dict on a successful append.
- [ ] `completion_sidecar.emit()` leaves `sidecar_reviewed_at` unset when the append fails.
- [ ] `completion_sidecar.emit()` stamps `sidecar_emitted` as `true` on a successful append.
- [ ] `completion_sidecar.emit()` stamps `sidecar_emitted` as `false` when the append fails.
- [ ] `_append_sidecar_retrying` returns the timestamp from `append_event`.
- [ ] `completion_sidecar.latest_verdict_timestamp` returns the newest sidecar's filename timestamp.
- [ ] `completion_sidecar.latest_verdict_timestamp` returns `None` when the ticket has no sidecar.
- [ ] The completion index record carries `sidecar_reviewed_at` after a terminal run.
- [ ] The completion index record carries `sidecar_emitted` after a terminal run.
- [ ] `_gate_sidecar_fields` returns an empty dict for gate type `code_review`.
- [ ] `gate_status` on a `code_review` job omits the `findings` key.
- [ ] A `plan_review` job's `findings` object still reports `sidecar_type` as `REVIEW_RESULT`.
- [ ] A `plan_review` job's `findings` object still reports `readable` as `true` for a current sidecar.
- [ ] A completion sidecar whose timestamp differs from the record's reports `readable` as `false`.
- [ ] A completion job in `running` state reports reason `run-running`.
- [ ] `gate_runs.py` stays under the 800-line module cap.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports no new entries.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports no increased entries.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` reports no new entries.
- [ ] `make lint` exits zero.
- [ ] `make typecheck` exits zero.
